form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 걷다 (to walk).
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so it becomes 걸어요.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times ten, 100

example.en: There are a hundred people in the park.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place with 있다 (there is).
form.why: 있다 (there is) uses 에 for the place: 공원에 있어요. 에서 is for places where an action happens.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times a hundred, 1,000

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
1,000 is just 천 (no 일 before it)
을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 주다 (to give).
form.why: 주다 + -었어요 shortens to 줬어요.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times a thousand, 10,000

example.en: I bought the gift for 10,000 won.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)
Korean counts big numbers in units of 만 (10,000)

form.q_en: Pick the Korean word for 10,000.
form.why: Korean has its own unit for 10,000: 만. It is never 십천 or 열천 ('ten thousand').

ko_meaning_en: The unit of Korean money

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is the won'.
form.why: 원 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: What you pay with when you buy things

example.en: I don't have any money now.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'money' with 없다 (to not have).
form.why: With 있다/없다, the thing you have or lack takes 이/가. 돈 ends in a consonant, so use 이.

ko_meaning_en: This day, the day it is now

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 'today'.
form.why: 오늘 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the topic marker is 은. 는 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The day before today

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that fits 'yesterday'.
form.why: 어제 (yesterday) needs the past tense: 만나다 → 만났어요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after today

tokens.note: the present tense can talk about the near future

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you go.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the destination takes 에: 학교에 가요.

ko_meaning_en: This very moment

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
오 + 아요 → 와요; in Korean, rain 'comes'

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 + -아요 shortens to 와요. Korean says rain 'comes': 비가 와요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 때부터 어떤 때까지의 동안, 또는 60분
ko_meaning_en: The length between two moments, or 60 minutes

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
rising intonation makes it a question

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'two' before 시간 (hours).
form.why: 시간 (hours) uses native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before it: 두 시간.

ko_meaning: 해가 뜨고 하루가 시작되는 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The time when the sun rises and the day begins, or the meal eaten then

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)
past tense, polite (-었어요); rising intonation = question

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'breakfast' the object.
form.why: 아침 ends in a consonant, so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 하루의 가운데 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The middle of the day, or the meal eaten then

example.en: I go to a restaurant at lunchtime.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you go.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the place you go to takes 에: 식당에 가요.

ko_meaning: 해가 지고 밤이 되기 전의 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The time after sunset before night, or the meal eaten then

example.en: I want to have dinner with my family.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'with'.
form.why: 하고 means 'with' (or 'and'): 가족하고 = with my family.

ko_meaning_en: The dark time after the sun sets

example.en: The stars are pretty at night.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
예쁘다 drops ㅡ: 예쁘 + 어요 → 예뻐요

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 예쁘다 (to be pretty).
form.why: 예쁘다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 예뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: The bright time when the sun is up

example.en: The child plays in the park during the day.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right form for 'during the day'.
form.why: Time words take 에: 낮에 (during the day). 에서 is for places, not times.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Sunday

example.en: I go to the office on Monday.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 가다 (to go).
form.why: 가다 + -아요 shortens to 가요 (the two ㅏ sounds merge).

ko_meaning_en: The day after Monday

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is Tuesday'.
form.why: 화요일 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Tuesday

example.en: I have an exam on Wednesday.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'on Wednesday'.
form.why: Days of the week take 에 for 'on': 수요일에 (on Wednesday).

ko_meaning_en: The day after Wednesday

example.en: I study at the library on Thursday.

tokens.note: 에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 공부하다 (to study).
form.why: 하다 verbs end in 해요 in the polite present: 공부하다 → 공부해요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Thursday

example.en: I watch a movie on Friday night.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'movie' the object.
form.why: 영화 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Friday

example.en: I want to go to the mountains on Saturday.

form.q_en: Pick the right form for 'want to go'.
form.why: 'Want to' is the verb stem + -고 싶어요: 가고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Saturday

example.en: I rest at home on Sunday.

tokens.note: 에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you rest.
form.why: 쉬다 (to rest) is an action, so the place takes 에서: 집에서 쉬어요. 에 is for where you go or where something is.

ko_meaning_en: Saturday and Sunday

example.en: I hang out with my friends on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 놀다 (to hang out).
form.why: 놀다 has the vowel ㅗ, so it takes -아요: 놀아요.

ko_meaning_en: Seven days, from Monday to Sunday

example.en: I exercise three times a week.

tokens.note: 셋 becomes 세 before a counter
번 = counter for how many times

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'three' before 번 (times).
form.why: 번 (times) uses native numbers, and 셋 becomes 세 before a counter: 세 번.

ko_meaning_en: The day you were born

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
no 의 needed: 엄마 생일 = mom's birthday

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'on the birthday'.
form.why: A day or time takes 에 for 'on': 생일에 (on the birthday). 에서 is for places.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting years

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic; 일 년 sounds like [일련]
열둘 becomes 열두 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number for 'one year'.
form.why: 년 is counted with Sino-Korean numbers: 일 년, 이 년. Native 한/하나 are not used with 년.

ko_meaning: 일 년의 열두 달을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to name the twelve months of a year

form.q_en: How do you say 'June'? (My birthday is in June.)
form.why: June is 유월: 육 drops its ㄱ before 월. October is likewise 시월, not 십월.

ko_meaning: 몇 시인지 시간을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to tell what hour it is

form.q_en: Pick the right number for 'seven o'clock'.
form.why: Hours use native numbers: 일곱 시. Sino-Korean 칠 is used for minutes, as in 칠 분.

ko_meaning: 시간의 작은 단위, 육십 분이 한 시간
ko_meaning_en: A small unit of time; sixty minutes make one hour

tokens.note: 셋 becomes 세 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number for '3:10'.
form.why: Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 분. Native 열 is for hours, as in 열 시.

ko_meaning_en: Each day; on all days

example.en: My younger sibling drinks milk every day.

form.q_en: Say 'every day' correctly.
form.why: 매일 is an adverb, so it takes no particle: 매일 마셔요, not 매일에.

ko_meaning_en: A place where people live

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where someone is

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at home'.
form.why: 있다 'to be (somewhere)' uses 에 for the place. 을/를 mark objects, and 의 means 'of'.

ko_meaning_en: A place where students learn from teachers

form.q_en: The child studies at school. Pick the particle.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (studying) happens. 에 is for where you go or where something is.

ko_meaning_en: A place where people work to earn money

example.en: My older sister goes to the office in the morning.

form.q_en: My older sister works at a company. Pick the particle.
form.why: 에서 marks where an action (working) happens. 에 is for where you go, as in 회사에 가요.

ko_meaning: 아픈 사람을 의사가 고쳐 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where doctors treat sick people

example.en: Grandpa went to the hospital yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'to the hospital'.
form.why: 가다 uses 에 for the destination; 에서 is for where an action happens. 가/를 only follow a vowel, and 병원 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A place that sells things

example.en: I buy bread at the shop.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the shop'.
form.why: 에서 marks where an action (buying) happens. 을/은 are forms for after a consonant, but 가게 ends in a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you pay and eat meals

example.en: I eat lunch at a restaurant with a friend.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at a restaurant'.
form.why: Eating is an action, so the place takes 에서. 를 is only used after a vowel, and 식당 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you keep or take out money

example.en: There is money in the bank.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: Ask 'Where is the bank?' Pick the particle.
form.why: 은행 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을/를 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: A place where many kinds of goods are bought and sold

example.en: There are a lot of people at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the market'.
form.why: 에 marks the place where something is: 시장에. 을/를 mark objects, and 가 cannot follow a consonant.

ko_meaning: 사람들이 쉬거나 놀 수 있는 넓은 곳
ko_meaning_en: A large open place where people can rest or play

example.en: The dog plays in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 놀다 'to play'.
form.why: 놀다 has ㅗ in its stem, so it takes -아요: 놀아요.

ko_meaning: 책을 읽거나 빌릴 수 있는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where you can read or borrow books

example.en: The student reads a book at the library.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the library'.
form.why: Reading happens at the library, so use 에서. 가/를 only follow a vowel, and 도서관 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 지금 있는 곳에서 다른 곳으로 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: To move from where you are to another place

example.en: I'm going to the sea tomorrow.

tokens.note: present tense can describe a plan

form.q_en: I went to the sea yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense. 가 + 았어요 shortens to 갔어요.

ko_meaning_en: To move from another place to here

example.en: My friend comes to my house.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 오다.
form.why: 오 + 아요 shortens to 와요.

ko_meaning: 사람이나 물건이 어디에 자리하다, 또는 가지다
ko_meaning_en: For a person or thing to be in a place; or to have something

tokens.note: with 있다, what you have takes 이/가

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'a dog' in 'Grandma has a dog'.
form.why: With 있다 'to have', the thing you have takes 이/가, not 을/를. 개 ends in a vowel, so 가.

en: to not be there; to not have
ko_meaning_en: To not be there; to not have

form.q_en: Say 'I don't have time today.'
form.why: The opposite of 있다 is its own word, 없다. Korean does not say 안 있어요 for 'don't have'.

ko_meaning_en: To make your home in a place and spend your life there

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'in Korea'.
form.why: 살다 takes 에 for the place you live (에서 also works). 살다 has no object, and 가/를 only follow a vowel.

ko_meaning: 밤에 눈을 감고 몸과 마음이 쉬다
ko_meaning_en: To close your eyes and let your body and mind rest, usually at night

form.q_en: The baby doesn't sleep at night. Pick the word that makes the verb negative.
form.why: To make a verb negative, put 안 right before it: 안 자요.

ko_meaning_en: To open your eyes and wake up from sleep

example.en: My older brother gets up at six every day.

form.q_en: My brother got up at six today. Pick the past form.
form.why: 일어나 + 았어요 shortens to 일어났어요.

ko_meaning_en: To make your body or things clean with water

example.en: My younger sibling washes their hands.

form.q_en: Politely ask someone: 'Please wash your hands.'
form.why: After a stem ending in a consonant, -(으)세요 becomes -으세요: 씻 + 으세요.

ko_meaning_en: To put clothes on your body

example.en: My older sister wore pants today.

form.q_en: Which thing do you 입다 'wear'?
form.why: 입다 is for clothes worn on the body, like 바지. A hat uses 쓰다 and shoes use 신다.

ko_meaning_en: To rest your bottom on a chair or the floor

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 앉다.
form.why: 앉 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 앉아요. The spelling keeps ㅈ, even though it sounds like [안자요].

ko_meaning_en: To take in people or things with your eyes

example.en: I watch a movie on the weekend.

form.q_en: I watched a movie yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense. 보 + 았어요 shortens to 봤어요.

ko_meaning_en: To take in sounds with your ears

example.en: My younger sibling listens to music.

tokens.note: irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 듣다.
form.why: 듣다 is irregular: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel, so 듣 + 어요 = 들어요.

ko_meaning_en: To express your thoughts out loud with your mouth

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 말하다.
form.why: 하다 verbs always become -해요 in the present: 말하다 → 말해요.

ko_meaning_en: To look at writing and understand its meaning

example.en: Grandpa reads the newspaper every day.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the newspaper'.
form.why: 신문 is the object and ends in a consonant, so it takes 을 (를 follows a vowel).

ko_meaning_en: To put letters down with a pencil or pen

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 쓰다.
form.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ before -어요: 쓰 + 어요 = 써요.

ko_meaning_en: To learn and practice things you don't know

form.q_en: Say 'I want to study Korean.'
form.why: -고 싶어요 attaches straight to the stem: 공부하 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 돈을 벌기 위해 어떤 일을 하다
ko_meaning_en: To do a job to earn money

example.en: The doctor works at the hospital.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: The doctor worked at the hospital yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 하다 verbs make the past with 했어요: 일하다 → 일했어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람과 같은 곳에서 얼굴을 보다
ko_meaning_en: To see another person face to face in the same place

example.en: I meet a friend on Saturday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'a friend'.
form.why: In Korean, 만나다 takes an object: 친구를 만나요. 친구 ends in a vowel, so 를, not 을.

ko_meaning_en: To give money and get something

example.en: I bought flowers for Mom's birthday.

tokens.note: 의 'of' is often dropped: 엄마 생일 = Mom's birthday

form.q_en: Pick the past form of 사다.
form.why: 사 has ㅏ, so it takes -았어요, and 사 + 았어요 shortens to 샀어요.

ko_meaning: 내 물건을 다른 사람이 가지게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To let another person have something of yours

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 주다.
form.why: 주 + 어요 shortens to 줘요.

en: to be big; to be tall
ko_meaning_en: To be larger or taller than usual

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 크다.
form.why: 크다 drops ㅡ before -어요: 크 + 어요 = 커요.

ko_meaning_en: To be smaller or shorter than usual

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 작다.
form.why: 작 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 작아요.

en: to be many; to be a lot
ko_meaning_en: For a number or amount to be more than usual

example.en: I have a lot of homework today.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'homework'.
form.why: 많다 describes the subject, so use the subject particle; 숙제 ends in a vowel, so 가.

en: to be few; to be little
ko_meaning_en: For a number or amount to be less than usual

example.en: There are few people in the library.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 적다.
form.why: 적 has ㅓ, not ㅏ or ㅗ, so it takes -어요: 적어요.

ko_meaning: 한쪽 끝에서 다른 쪽 끝까지가 멀다
ko_meaning_en: For the distance from one end to the other to be great

form.q_en: Yesterday's class was long. Pick the past form.
form.why: 길다 has ㅣ in its stem, so it takes -었어요: 길었어요. 길어요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To be nice and pleasing

form.q_en: Say 'I like kimchi' with an object (김치를).
form.why: 좋다 cannot take an object (을/를). With 김치를, use 좋아하다: 좋아해요.

ko_meaning_en: To not be good

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 나쁘다.
form.why: 나쁘다 drops ㅡ. The syllable before it (나) has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 나빠요.

ko_meaning_en: To look nice; to be lovely to look at

example.en: My older sister's clothes are pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 예쁘다.
form.why: 예쁘다 drops ㅡ. The syllable before it (예) has no ㅏ or ㅗ, so it takes -어요: 예뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: To be enjoyable and make you feel good

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'studying'.
form.why: 재미있다 describes the subject, so 공부 takes the subject particle; it ends in a vowel, so 가.

ko_meaning: 할 일이 많아서 쉴 시간이 없다
ko_meaning_en: To have so much to do that there is no time to rest

form.q_en: Dad was busy yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 바쁘다 drops ㅡ and takes ㅏ (from 바): 바빠요, and in the past 바빴어요.

ko_meaning: 그날의 비, 바람, 해 같은 하늘의 상태
ko_meaning_en: The state of the sky that day, such as rain, wind and sun

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the weather'.
form.why: 날씨 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가 (이 follows a consonant). 를/을 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: For the air to feel hot to your body

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 덥다.
form.why: 덥다 is irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -어요, so it is 더워요.

ko_meaning_en: For the air to feel cold to your body

form.q_en: It was very cold yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 추워요 in the present, 추웠어요 in the past. 어제 needs the past.

ko_meaning_en: To be slightly warm in a pleasant way

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 따뜻하다.
form.why: 하다 words become 해요 in the present: 따뜻하다 → 따뜻해요.

en: to be cool; to be refreshing
ko_meaning_en: To be pleasantly cool

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the wind'.
form.why: 바람 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이, not 가. 을/를 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: The warm season that comes after winter

example.en: There are a lot of flowers in spring.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
the ㅎ in 많 is silent here

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'in (a time)'.
form.why: 에 marks the time when something happens. 에서 is for the place of an action, and 을/가 do not fit here.

ko_meaning: 봄 다음에 오는 아주 더운 계절
ko_meaning_en: The very hot season that comes after spring

tokens.note: 에 marks a time, 는 makes it the topic

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'in summer' (a time).
form.why: 에 marks a time such as a season, and 는 makes it the topic. 에서 marks where an action happens, not when.

ko_meaning_en: The cool season that comes after summer

example.en: I want to go to the mountains in autumn.

form.q_en: Pick the form that completes 'want to go'.
form.why: To say 'want to', add -고 to the verb stem and then 싶어요: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 가을 다음에 오는 아주 추운 계절
ko_meaning_en: The very cold season that comes after autumn

tokens.note: 눈 also means 'eye'; here it means snow

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 + -아요 shortens to 와요. 'Snow comes' is how Korean says 'it snows'.

ko_meaning: 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울 중 하나
ko_meaning_en: One of spring, summer, autumn, and winter

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 계절.
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object. 계절 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so use 을; 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The color of a ripe apple

ko_meaning_en: To feel hurt inside because something bad happened

form.q_en: Pick the correct past polite form of 슬프다.
form.why: 슬프다 drops ㅡ in the past too: 슬프 + 었어요 → 슬펐어요.

ko_meaning_en: To feel glad and very good inside

form.q_en: Write a warm wish: 'Always be happy!'
form.why: 하다 words take -세요 directly: 행복하 + 세요 → 행복하세요.

ko_meaning: 싫은 일이 있어서 기분이 많이 나빠지다
ko_meaning_en: To feel really bad because something unpleasant happened

form.q_en: Pick the correct form: 'Why is Dad angry?'
form.why: 화나 + 았어요 contracts to 화났어요. Koreans use this past form to say someone is angry now.

ko_meaning_en: To feel worn out after doing a lot

example.en: I'm tired every day these days.

form.q_en: Say 'I'm not tired now.'
form.why: Put 안 right before a verb or adjective to say 'not'.

ko_meaning_en: To feel bad because your body is not well

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 아프다.
form.why: 아프다 drops ㅡ, and because the syllable before has ㅏ it takes -아요: 아파요.

ko_meaning: 목이 아프고 코에서 물이 나오는 병
ko_meaning_en: An illness where your throat hurts and your nose runs

example.en: My younger sibling caught a cold.

tokens.note: 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold
past tense, polite: 걸리 + 었어요 → 걸렸어요

form.q_en: Pick the particle: 'to catch a cold'.
form.why: Korean says 감기에 걸리다 (literally 'be caught by a cold'), so use 에, not 를.

ko_meaning_en: Something you take when you are sick

example.en: I took medicine in the morning.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the verb Koreans use for taking medicine.
form.why: In Korean you 'eat' medicine: 약을 먹다.

ko_meaning: 병원에서 아픈 사람을 낫게 해 주는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person at a hospital who makes sick people better

example.en: My older sister is a doctor.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'is' after 의사.
form.why: 의사 ends in a vowel, so use 예요. 이에요 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 일을 하지 않고 몸을 편하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To stop working and let your body relax

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: It happened yesterday. Pick the correct past form of 쉬다.
form.why: 쉬 + 었어요 = 쉬었어요 (ㅟ does not contract). 어제 needs the past, so 쉬어요 is wrong.

ko_meaning_en: A fully grown person

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle: 'Adults drink coffee.'
form.why: 어른 ends in a consonant, so the topic particle is 은, not 는. 을 marks an object.

ko_meaning_en: A person who works at a company

example.en: My dad is an office worker.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'is' after 회사원.
form.why: 회사원 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so use 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The word used to call a person or thing

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
뭐 is the short spoken form of 무엇

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 이름.
form.why: 이름 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이. 가 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The number of years since you were born

form.q_en: Pick the word Koreans use to say someone is old.
form.why: Koreans say 나이가 많다 'to have many years' for being old.

ko_meaning: 두 사람이 한 가족이 되는 것
ko_meaning_en: Two people becoming one family

form.q_en: Say 'My older sister got married.'
form.why: 결혼 + 하다 = 결혼하다, and the past polite form of 하다 is 했어요.

ko_meaning_en: Telling about something in words

form.q_en: 'I talked with a friend.' Pick the particle for 이야기.
form.why: 이야기 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를: 이야기를 하다 'to talk'.

ko_meaning_en: Something you sing along with music

example.en: My younger sibling sings a song.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 부르다 'to sing'.
form.why: 부르다 is 르 irregular: 부르 + 어요 → 불러요. 불어요 comes from 불다 'to blow'.

ko_meaning_en: Asking about something you don't know

form.q_en: 'The student asked a question.' Pick the particle.
form.why: 질문 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을: 질문을 하다 'to ask a question'.

ko_meaning_en: What you say back to a question

tokens.note: 안 before a verb makes it negative

form.q_en: Say 'The child doesn't answer.'
form.why: 안 goes right before 하다: 대답을 안 해요. 않 is used only in -지 않다.

ko_meaning_en: The language Korean people use

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that goes before 싶어요.
form.why: -고 싶어요 attaches to the verb stem: 배우 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: A country in East Asia

example.en: I want to go to Korea.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place you go to

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you want to go.
form.why: 에 marks the place you go to. 이 marks a subject, 의 means 'of', and 와 is only used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A place like Korea or the United States

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
크다 drops ㅡ: 크 + 어요 → 커요

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'country' the subject.
form.why: 가 marks the subject after a vowel; 이 is used after a consonant. 를 marks an object and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: A country that is not your own

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where he works.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (working) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: The language used in the US and the UK

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'English' the object.
form.why: 를 marks the object after a vowel; 을 is used after a consonant. 에 and 가 do not mark an object.

ko_meaning_en: Sounds or talk that people make with their mouth

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant
듣다 is irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'words' the object.
form.why: 말 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: Moving your body to stay healthy

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'exercise' the object.
form.why: 운동 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: A story on screen that you watch at a cinema or on TV

example.en: I watched a movie on the weekend.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 보다 (to watch).
form.why: 보다 has ㅗ, so it takes -았어요, and 보 + 았어요 shortens to 봤어요.

ko_meaning_en: Songs or sounds of instruments that you hear

tokens.note: 저 is the polite word for 'I'; 는 marks the topic
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 좋아해요 (to like).
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object, and 음악 ends in a consonant, so use 을. 를 follows a vowel; 에 and 이 do not fit.

ko_meaning: 다른 곳이나 나라에 가서 보고 즐기는 것
ko_meaning_en: Going to another place or country to see and enjoy it

example.en: I want to go on a trip with my family.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle: '여행 ___ 가다' means 'to go on a trip'.
form.why: Korean says 여행을 가다. 여행 ends in a consonant, so 을, not 를. 이 and 에서 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: A picture taken with a camera

example.en: I took a photo with my friend.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'photo' the object.
form.why: 사진 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: To spend time having fun

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Yesterday the children played outside. Pick the past form.
form.why: 놀다 has ㅗ in its stem, so it takes -았어요: 놀았어요. 놀아요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To go on foot, one step at a time

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
걷다 is irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 걷다 (to walk).
form.why: 걷다 is irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 어요 → 걸어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go very fast on foot

example.en: The dog runs in the park.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 달리다 (to run).
form.why: When the stem ends in 리, 리 + 어요 combine into 려요: 달려요.

ko_meaning: 노래를 하다. 또는 이름을 말해서 오게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To sing a song; or to say a name to make someone come

example.en: My older sister sings a song.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 부르다 (to sing).
form.why: 부르다 is a 르 irregular verb: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 부르 + 어요 → 불러요.

ko_meaning_en: To make a photo with a camera

example.en: I want to take a photo here.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 싶어요 (want to).
form.why: To say 'want to', add -고 싶어요 to the verb stem: 찍 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: To give something and receive money for it

example.en: They sell fruit at the market.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 팔다.
form.why: 팔다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 팔 + 아요 → 팔아요.

ko_meaning_en: The price is low

example.en: Fruit is cheap at the market.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 싸다 (to be cheap).
form.why: When the stem ends in ㅏ, the 아 of -아요 drops: 싸 + 아요 → 싸요.

ko_meaning_en: The price is high

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 비싸다.
form.why: Past tense: 비싸 + 았어요 shortens to 비쌌어요.

ko_meaning: 물건을 살 때 내는 돈, 값
ko_meaning_en: The money you pay when you buy something; the cost

example.en: How much is it? (What is the price?)

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'price' the subject.
form.why: 가격 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을 and 에 do not fit.

ko_meaning: 고마울 때나 축하할 때 주는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you give to say thanks or to celebrate

example.en: My friend gave me a present on my birthday.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 주다 (to give).
form.why: 주다 has ㅜ, so it takes -었어요, and 주 + 었어요 shortens to 줬어요.

ko_meaning_en: Much more than usual

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'very' before an adjective.
form.why: 아주 is an adverb, so it can go before the adjective 맛있어요. 큰, 커요 and 크다 are forms of the adjective 크다 and cannot do that.

ko_meaning_en: In a small amount or degree

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'a little' before a verb.
form.why: 조금 is an adverb that goes before the verb. 적은, 적어요 and 적다 are forms of the adjective 적다 and cannot describe 마셨어요.

ko_meaning_en: In a large number or amount

example.en: I slept a lot on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the adverb form of 많다 (to be many).
form.why: 많이 is the adverb ('a lot') that describes the verb 왔어요. 많은, 많아요 and 많다 are adjective forms.

ko_meaning_en: Two or more, at the same time and place

example.en: I eat lunch together with my friend.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 같이 for 'together with a friend'.
form.why: 하고 (or 와/과) + 같이 means 'together with'. 를, 의 and 에서 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: One more time

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: After a vowel stem, add -세요 directly: 오 + 세요 → 오세요 (please come).

ko_meaning_en: In a short time

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the adverb that means 'quickly'.
form.why: 빨리 is the adverb that describes how time goes. 빠른, 빨라요 and 빠르다 are forms of the adjective 빠르다.

ko_meaning_en: Slowly, without hurrying

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 말하다 (to speak).
form.why: The stem 말하- ends in a vowel, so add -세요 directly: 말하세요.

ko_meaning_en: Doing the same thing many times

example.en: I often go to the library.

tokens.note: 저 is the polite word for 'I'
에 marks the place you go to

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you go to.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the destination takes 에. 에서 is for where an action happens; 을 and 이 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: At all times

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 바쁘다 (to be busy).
form.why: 바쁘다 drops ㅡ, and the vowel before it is ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 바빠요.

ko_meaning_en: Before other people or things

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 씻다 (to wash).
form.why: The stem 씻- ends in a consonant, so add -으세요: 씻으세요.

ko_meaning: 지금도 계속, 또는 지금까지 안 되어서
ko_meaning_en: Even now; or not happened up to now

example.en: I haven't done my homework yet.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the word that makes the verb negative ('not yet').
form.why: 안 goes right before the verb to make it negative. 아니요 and 네 are answers ('no', 'yes'), and 없어 means 'there isn't'.

ko_meaning_en: Sooner than you thought; already

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'it is night'.
form.why: 밤 ends in a consonant, so use 이에요. 예요 is used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: Before much time passes; soon

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 has ㅗ, so it takes -아요, and 오 + 아요 shortens to 와요.

ko_meaning_en: Not now, but some time after

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 나중 mean 'later'.
form.why: 나중 is a time word and takes 에 to mean 'at a later time'. 이, 를 and 의 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: From a little while ago until now

example.en: The weather is cold these days.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 춥다 (to be cold).
form.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 춥 + 어요 → 추워요.

ko_meaning_en: Not hard to do

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 쉽다 (to be easy).
form.why: 쉽다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ changes to 우, so 쉽 + 었어요 → 쉬웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: Hard to do

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'not' before an adjective.
form.why: 안 + adjective means 'not': 안 어려워요 = it isn't difficult. 못 (cannot) is not used with adjectives, and 아니요/없어 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: The distance is short

example.en: The school is close to my home.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'from' here.
form.why: 에서 can mean 'from': 집에서 가까워요 = close from home. 을 and 의 do not fit, and 와 is only used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The distance is long

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 멀다.
form.why: 멀다 has ㅓ in the stem, so it takes -어요: 멀 + 어요 → 멀어요.

ko_meaning_en: Long from bottom to top

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'sky' the subject.
form.why: 하늘 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을 and 에 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: Short from bottom to top

example.en: The chair is a little low.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 낮다.
form.why: 낮다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 낮 + 아요 → 낮아요.

ko_meaning_en: It weighs a lot and is hard to lift

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 무겁다 (to be heavy).
form.why: 무겁다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 무겁 + 었어요 → 무거웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: It weighs little and is easy to lift

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 가볍다 (to be light).
form.why: 가볍다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 가볍 + 어요 → 가벼워요.

ko_meaning_en: Moving a lot in a short time

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 빠르다 (to be fast).
form.why: 빠르다 is a 르 irregular word: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 빠르 + 아요 → 빨라요.

ko_meaning_en: Taking a long time to move

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 느리다 (to be slow).
form.why: When the stem ends in 리, 리 + 어요 combine into 려요: 느려요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것을 배워서 머리에 가지고 있다
ko_meaning_en: To have learned something and keep it in your head

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 알다.
form.why: 알다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 알 + 아요 → 알아요.

ko_meaning_en: To not know something

example.en: I don't know that person's name.

form.q_en: Yesterday I didn't know. Pick the past form of 모르다.
form.why: 모르다 is 르-irregular: 모르 + 았어요 → 몰랐어요. 몰라요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To stay until a person or a time comes

example.en: I wait for my friend at the station.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person you wait for.
form.why: Korean says 'wait someone' with an object particle: 친구를 기다려요. 친구 ends in a vowel, so 를, not 을.

ko_meaning_en: To study something you do not know and come to know it

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 배우다 (to learn).
form.why: 배우다 has ㅜ, so it takes -어요, and 우 + 어요 combine into 워요: 배워요.

ko_meaning_en: To do the first part of something

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
native numbers are used for hours

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 시작하다.
form.why: Verbs ending in 하다 change 하 + 여요 into 해요: 시작해요.
